godbolt_skip: The symptom is the byte size and deflate ratio of the compiled object. Compiler Explorer panes show text disassembly; no pane can show an object's byte count, and none can run deflate. A link would show fxc, dxc and clang all succeeding, which published bare reads as 'cannot reproduce' -- the #2191 trap, and here without even #2191's partial value (there is no release-vs-debug distinction to demonstrate). A Clang pane was considered and rejected for the same reason: clang's HLSL path emits the same LLVM bitcode encoding, so it inherits the property by construction, but a text pane still cannot display it -- the claim would be asserted, not shown. The shareable repro is measure.py, committed in this directory, which recompiles the corpus and prints bytes/deflated/ratio; manual-case-compression.txt is its verified output.
summary: Confirmed and unchanged since v1.4.1907. dxc objects zip to 3.7x fxc's for the same shaders (fxc ratio 0.33 vs reporter's ~0.30; dxc -Qstrip_reflect 0.77 vs reporter's 0.80-0.85); raw sizes differ by 1.5%, so the whole gap is compressibility. The DXIL part alone deflates to 0.848/0.900 -- LLVM 3.7 bitcode is bit-packed and near entropy-dense where DXBC's SHEX is byte-aligned repetitive tokens (0.271). Half of BitMD's 2019 comment landed: reflection moved out of the module into STAT between v1.4.1907 and v1.5.2010, cutting corpus size 39% raw, but the bitcode's compressibility never moved (0.839 -> 0.851 -> 0.848). Division's 2022 question answered: PC dxc has no shader-object compression to disable -- zlib is used only by the PDB writer and the SRCI source part. Not a defect; a container-encoding decision.
title: Generated bytecode by dxc has very higher compression ratio
